To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The efficiency of label typing can be modeled by a linear function of the length of the label, the number of characters that can be typed before selection, and the average number of characters in a label; (2) The average number of characters per label on a page is a good predictor of typing efficiency, and (3) The number of characters that users can type before selection is a good predictor for the number of characters in an element label.
we have developed an approach to generate labels for elements on web pages that are efficient and meaningful to the users.

(1) the label generation process should be based on a combination of structural analysis, user history, and the efficiency model; (2) labels should be generated for the most important elements of the web page, which can be defined as those elements that are most frequently used and most frequently selected; and (3) the label generation should be done on the client side, as the server side is not aware of the user's history and the efficiency model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to generate efficient labels to facilitate accessibility.
how to generate labels for web elements, which will be both efficient for users and meaningful.
the problem of generating efficient labels for web elements that are difficult to label, and we have developed an efficient and effective solution to this problem.

the label selection approach is an effective way of providing web accessibility for users with a disability, but that the efficiency of label selection depends on the type of input device, and that the efficiency of the input device is affected by the label selection approach.
this paper is a very well written and researched study of the problems and possible solutions for generating efficient labels to facilitate Web accessibility.

the label typing approach is a viable method of selection for users with a disability, and that the generation of these labels can be achieved by using a combination of page structure and input device efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed and implemented a system that can generate labels that are efficient to select and meaningful to the users.

our approach is able to generate labels that are more efficient to select than labels that are generated by the page author, and more meaningful to the user than labels generated from the page structure alone.
we are trying to find a good compromise between the efficiency of the input device and the meaning of the label to the user.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a user history can provide a good estimate of the importance of elements on a web document, and that the efficiency model of input devices is a key factor in determining the best labels for a web page.
it is possible to generate labels that are both efficient for text input and meaningful, and this can be achieved with a simple model.

it is possible to use a variety of techniques, including structural analysis and user behavior analysis, to automatically generate a meaningful set of element labels that can improve the accessibility of a web page.
